segments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Twenty-Three. Construct on a given line at a given point an angle equal to a given angle. Given segment A B, point A on it, and angle D C E, we construct at point A on segment A B an angle equal to angle D C E.

subsegments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Twenty-Three. Construct on a given line at a given point an angle equal to a given angle. Given segment A B, point A on it, and angle D C E, we construct at point A on segment A B an angle equal to angle D C E.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: On lines C D and C E, take random points D and E, and construct segment D E. Then, from three segments equal to C D, D E, and C E, construct triangle A F G on segment A B so that A F equals C D, A G equals C E, and F G equals D E.

subsegments.text: On lines C D and C E, take random points D and E, and construct segment D E. Then, from three segments equal to C D, D E, and C E, construct triangle A F G on segment A B so that A F equals C D, A G equals C E, and F G equals D E.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: In triangles D C E and F A G, sides D C and C E equal sides F A and A G respectively, and base D E equals base F G. By side-side-side congruence, angle D C E equals angle F A G. Therefore on the given segment A B and at the given point A on it, angle F A G has been constructed equal to angle D C E, as was required to do.
